newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: President tackles property problem in Nicaragua.
newsitem.headline: President tackles property problem in Nicaragua.

text.p: Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman on Thursday launched an ambitious plan to resolve Nicaragua's private property problem by granting legal titles to 50 families who had received confiscated land.

Aleman's Liberal Alliance government, which took office on Jan. 10, plans to give property titles to 102,000 poor families who received confiscated land during the 1979-1990 left-wing Sandinista government, legalising their ownership.
But he plans to make wealthy Sandinistas who received confiscated property return or pay for it, hopefully ending confusion over property ownership in Nicaragua.

"On this historic day we begin the process of legalising the plots of land of thousands of humble men and women. With this we are sewing the seeds of social peace in Nicaragua," Aleman told reporters in Managua's poor Primavera area.
In a flurry of legislation before leaving office after their 1990 election loss to former President Violeta Chamorro, the Sandinistas parceled out more than 200,000 properties they had confiscated.

Conflicts between the current occupants and the former owners became a major sticking point in the reconciliation between the Sandinistas and the right-wing Liberals, and led to insecurity over land ownership.
Resolving the legal insecurity surrounding private property is one of the main demands of the Nicaraguan business community and foreign investors.
